I read everything via `git show origin/research/agent-architecture:<path>` and ran nothing, so behaviour below is from the code, not from execution.

## 1. dev/synth architecture

Commit a94a0d4 added six files (2,797 lines); 9cde4cc after it touches only `agent/`.

### scenario.py (972 lines): the seeded world generator

- **Entry point:** `generate(seed: int, dataset: str = "mixed") -> World` (l.335). It tries up to 200 sub-seeds, `random.Random(seed * 1009 + attempt + salt)` with `salt = index(dataset) * 7_000_003`, and returns the first draw the oracle accepts as unambiguous and whose decision matches the `no_bid` flag (l.969-971).
- **`_generate(seed, r, fixed) -> World`** (l.347) imports `oracle` to place traps around true values, e.g. a threshold one cent above the order value or a ceiling one piece short.
- **`profile(dataset, seed) -> dict`** (l.281) returns the features a dataset pins; everything else is drawn.
- **`GENERATION = 3`** (l.21) is recorded with each run; a seed means a different scenario across generations.
- **Dataclasses** (l.61-189): `Position`, `QA` (kinds: quantity, withdrawal, group, packaging, commitment, pool, bonus, setup, amendment, noise), `Req`, `Revision` (status current/superseded/draft/withdrawn), `Condition`, `Material`, `Mail` (`kind`, `reference`, `is_record`, `data`), `Tender`, `World` (with `senders()` and `current()`).
- **Number formatting:** `de(value, places=2)` and `plain(value)` (l.44, l.55) read a module-global `LOCALE[0]`, mutated per mail in `versions.send` (l.643). This is not thread-safe.

How many scenarios: unlimited seeds across 33 named datasets (`DATASETS`, l.244-278).

- `mixed`: every feature drawn at random.
- `public-like` and `no-bid`: every rule in play on five positions.
- `plain`: no clauses at all.
- `one-trap`: `TRAPS[seed % 22]` (l.232-243), one rule's trap on an otherwise plain tender.
- 28 single-oddness sets, e.g. `boundaries-met`, `boundaries-missed`, `minute-precision`, `long-chains`, `decoy-flood`, `only-fakes`, `many-revisions`, `release-taken-back`, `strange-ids`, `foreign-notations`, `metal-maze`, `everything-weird`.

What varies in the data:

- **Feature flags** (l.350-359): `no_bid` 15 %, `satz`, `shared`, `usable`, `amend`, `withdrawn`, `fx`, `unit100`, `approval` in none/plain/cond_pass/cond_fail, `groups`, `metal`, `windows`, `packaging`, `commitment` in none/applies/ceiling/material, `pool` in none/largest_remainder/rest_to_largest, `bonus`, `setup`.
- **Surface forms** (l.362): `opaque_ids`, `tight_dates` (hours apart, or `"minutes"`), `small_quantities`.
- **Identity:** scenario date 2025-2027, reference formats (`_reference`, l.195), company and domain (`*.example`), director, mailbox local part.
- **Structure:** 3-5 positions (1, 8 or 12 in some datasets), position-number schemes, requirement-id schemes, revision naming (letters, 01.., 2.0.., roman, opaque `R-1234`), 2-3 revisions plus optional withdrawn and draft ones.
- **ERP:** material-number schemes (`_material_number`, l.204), catalogue-group schemes, 7-10 extra groups so a broad search is refused.
- **Mail:** 10-16 noise mails (40-60 in flood), inbox/archive split (l.954), per-mail number notation de/en (ch/fr in some datasets) declared in the body (l.644).

### sites.py (821 lines): four mock sites

- **Framework:** stdlib `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer`, one server per site on 127.0.0.1.
- **Ports:** `start(app, first_port=0) -> list[ThreadingHTTPServer]` (l.811) uses free ports by default; `serve --port 8800` uses 8800-8803. It sets `site.url`.
- **Classes:** `App(world)` (l.120) holds `skin`, `signed`, `tans`, `tan_mails`, `hits` and `clock()` (the scenario clock). `Site` (l.150) is the base for `TenderSite`, `SupplierSite`, `ErpSite`, `MailSite`. `Handler` (l.772) uses a cookie `sid_<role>`.
- **Look:** `Skin(random.Random((world.seed + 1) * 7919))` (l.67-88) depends on the seed only, not the dataset. It draws:
  - paging (next/numbered/more) and page size 4-6;
  - list style (table/cards) and date notation (de/iso/UTC+2 offset);
  - bid-form flow (wizard, wizard_each, single) and material input (text/select);
  - revision status display (badge/tooltip/text) and spec style (table/prose);
  - ERP layout (tabs/sections) and mail opening (page/pane);
  - `qa_site` (tender, tender, supplier) and `qa_order`;
  - default offer type (`neben` or empty), confirm dialog, empty-search behaviour;
  - hazards, each at 60 %: flaky, timeout, modal, inject, gate;
  - brief headings, one of two German label vocabularies (`WORDS`, l.47), and product name plus site id per role from 4 options (`PRODUCTS`, l.37), including neutral `site-1`..`site-4`.
- **Login and nuisances** (`Site.dispatch`, l.217):
  - `/login` POST with per-process random credentials (`secrets`, l.156, not seeded).
  - `/consent` cookie wall.
  - `/zugang` access-number gate on supplier and ERP.
  - ERP session expiry after 40 hits (l.264).
  - A flaky page on hits 5 and 23 (l.267).
  - A newsletter overlay.
  - A hidden prompt-injection div in mails (l.729).
- **Tender routes:** `/` (search, 3 per page, 4 decoy tenders), `/a/<tid>`, `/a/<tid>/unterlagen[/1..3]` (1 is the bill of quantities), `/a/<tid>/fragen` (only if `qa_site == "tender"`), `/a/<tid>/angebot?schritt=N`, `/a/<tid>/angebot/pruefen` with `aktion=tan|abgeben`.
- **Supplier routes:** `/` (document search), `/dok/<id>?rev=` (opens `revisions[0]`, the oldest, l.607; requirements 2 per page), `/klarstellungen[/<tid>]` when the Q&A lives there.
- **ERP routes:** `/suche?q=` (empty refused, more than 20 hits refused, l.661), `/material/<nr>?tab=technik|dispo|bestand|logistik|preise`.
- **Mail routes:** `/?ordner=inbox|archive&q=` (AND search, per folder), `/nachricht/<mid>` or pane `?nachricht=`.
- **Bid form:** company, VAT and email; offer type radio with alternative offer listed first; positions with 8 fields plus an omit box; "add position" trap; own-terms checkbox trap. `collect()` (l.456) builds the answer and blocks signing on problems.
- **TAN:** `secrets.token_hex(4).upper()`, valid 5 minutes, each request invalidates earlier ones, delivered as a mail in the inbox (l.515-525). The signed bid is stored in `App.signed`; there is no HTTP back door.

How ids and URLs reach the agent: only through the run JSON built by `run.py` (`access[].siteId/url/credentials`, shuffled) and the brief's shuffled site list.

### oracle.py (412 lines): independent answer, scorer, calc cross-check

- **Record selection:**
  - `authority(world, kind)` (l.34): latest record with exact reference, authorised sender, `date <= scenario`.
  - `entry(world, kind, **where)`.
  - `qa_key(world, kind, position)`.
- **Per-position derivation:**
  - `quantity` (rules 1, 13).
  - `pieces` (17).
  - `requirement` (2, 14, 20).
  - `material` (3, 10; raises on two matches).
  - `base_price` (4, 22).
- **Order level:**
  - `order_value` (16).
  - `discount(world, value)` (5, 16).
  - `split_cents(amount, weights, rule="largest_remainder")` (l.136).
- **`solve(world, detail=False) -> dict`** (l.156):
  - Any missing material gives no_bid; the discount is the plain approval's percent, or 0 if the approval is conditional.
  - Otherwise unit price is `base*f_base + surcharge*f_sur + (setup + cartons - credit)/count`, rounded once (l.220).
  - Lead time uses pooled demand against free stock, then a commitment override (l.221-226).
- **`score(world, expected, got) -> dict`** (l.255): rule 29 weights, positions matched by number, extras cost one position's share. No-bid cases score 75/5/5/15.
- **`via_calc(world) -> dict`** (l.327) feeds the same world through `agent/calc.py`.

Two caveats in the scorer:
- The docstring cites `docs/scoring.md`, which does not exist on the branch.
- The two "when present" 5-point checks are the author's interpretation (l.7-9): the quantity of the position behind a withdrawn answer, and the surcharge of positions with windowed indices.

### run.py (436 lines): the CLI

| Subcommand | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `check --seeds 300 --first 0 --forms 60` | Compares oracle with `via_calc`; does an HTTP form round trip via `Client`/`enter()` (l.127-179) that must score 100 |
| `show --seed N` | Prints features, look and expected answer |
| `serve --seed N --port 8800` | Serves the sites, writes `dev/synth/.run-N.json`, prints the score when a bid is signed |
| `agent --seeds 0-5 --minutes 20 --version --note` | Runs the agent per seed and records the score |
| `export --seeds --out` | Writes plain JSON per scenario including labels and expected answer to `dev/synth/data/` |
| `report --version` | Mean quality by feature and look, most frequent misses |

All except `report` take `--dataset`.

How it stands in for the platform:

- **Brief:** `brief(app)` (l.52) is an English task brief with reference, scenario time, company, VAT, director and shuffled site list, followed by `rules.md` verbatim and submission instructions.
- **Run object:** `build_run(app, seconds=1200)` (l.94) returns `{run_id: None, brief, access, submission: {kind: "site", siteId, url}, answer_schema, started_at, expires_at}`.
- **No API server:** the run is passed only as `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`. There is no `/v1/runs/current`, no run token, no `llm_proxy_url`.
- **No schema validation:** `answer_schema.json` is only handed to the agent; the bid form's `collect()` is the sole validation.
- **Scoring:** `judge(app, expected)` (l.106) calls `oracle.score` on `App.signed`, turns an alternative offer into a wrong decision, and reports form traps (own terms, omitted, extra rows, TAN requests, company and contact correctness) and seconds.

How it drives the agent (`run_agent`, l.326-358):

- It runs `subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "python", "agent.py"], cwd=ROOT/"agent", ...)` with timeout minutes*60+120.
- It removes `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` and `CHALLENGE_API_URL` from the environment.
- It sets `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, `TRACE_DIR=agent/traces/synth-<seed>-<ts>`, `HEADLESS` (default 1), `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy`, and defaults `QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1`, `QWEN_API_KEY=local`.
- It appends a record to `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl`: quality, parts, wrong fields, features, look, request counts, commit, dirty flag, and any `AGENT_|LLM_|THINKING|MAX_STEPS|SPEC_` variables.
- `cmd_agent` first probes the model proxy (l.363).

`rules.md` (29 lines) is identical to the 29 rules in the live `rfq.md`. `answer_schema.json` matches the live schema.

## 2. Rule coverage

"Where" refers to `scenario.py` unless noted.

| # | Rule | Covered | Where and notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Quantity, latest clarification | yes | l.500-515: older, governing and future-dated change |
| 2 | Revision marked current | yes | l.481-490 superseded, withdrawn, draft; site opens oldest first (`sites.py` l.607); status as badge, tooltip or text |
| 3 | Exact active material, else no_bid | yes | l.700-709: inactive or blocked exact twin, unamended match, old-revision match, 2-4 near misses |
| 4 | Valid condition, highest scale | yes | l.763-782: past, current, future conditions shuffled; cuts at own quantity, max+1 and pooled sum |
| 5 | Director approval, exact tender | yes | l.916-943: superseded, future, look-alike reference, colleague's note, request mail |
| 6 | Stock vs production lead time | yes | l.750-755: free stock short while blocked stock would cover |
| 7 | Total | yes | `oracle.py` l.232 |
| 8 | Decision | yes | `no_bid` flag; alternative-offer default in the form |
| 9 | Partial submission | partly | Omit box and score exist; nothing forces or tests omission |
| 10 | Finding records | partly | Over-20 and empty ERP search refused, AND mail search, archive folder; no F4 popup or transaction codes |
| 11 | Agent requirement | n/a | Not checkable by a harness |
| 12 | Konditionsgruppe clauses | yes | l.562-576, l.795-805: three scopes, replaced assignment (30 %), unused keys; same-material case only by chance |
| 13 | Withdrawn answers | yes | l.516-525; `future-withdrawal` dataset |
| 14 | Scoped amendments | yes | l.526-550: older, latest, future, other-revision; other revision is always `revisions[0]` |

# sim: a local mirror of the challenge's websites

Records the four public scouting websites through a browser and serves them again on this machine, so the agent
can be run offline, without the shared scouting login and as often as needed. Nothing here is part of the
submitted package (`agent/`); `atira test-run ./agent --dry-run` lists none of it.

What was recorded is website content. It stays in `sim/captured/` (gitignored) and never goes into the repo, the
package, tests, docs or prompts. The code in this folder holds no wording, markup or values of the websites: the
mirror takes all of that from the recording when it starts. Recording is ordinary signed-in use of the websites
with the scouting logins (pages, searches, the bid form); nothing is guessed at or probed.

## Use

From the repo root:

```sh
# 1. Record (about 30 minutes, once per team member; needs `atira login`)
HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python sim/drive.py serve &          # signed-in tabs on the four websites
uv run --project agent python sim/drive.py tender-portal crawl 200    # follow the links a website shows
uv run --project agent python sim/drive.py erp goto "/search?..."     # a search, a form, a gate: one action each
uv run --project agent python sim/drive.py - stop

# 2. Check the mirror against the recording
python3 -m unittest discover -s sim/tests                              # no browser, no model, about 2 s
HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python sim/tests/browser_check.py    # the agent's view, mirror vs website

# 3. Run the agent against the mirror (needs `atira models proxy` in another terminal)
dev/run-sim.sh v2 "what changed"
python3 sim/mirror.py                                                  # or just serve it and browse
```

## Keeping it complete and current

```sh
uv run --project agent python sim/refresh.py audit            # offline: what could be asked for but is not recorded
uv run --project agent python sim/refresh.py refresh --form   # ask the websites again; store what changed or is new
```

`audit` lists addresses the recorded pages link to, addresses an agent asked the mirror for, and bid-form choices
nobody walked. `refresh` fetches every recorded address and every gap from the live websites with the scouting
login, reports changed, new and gone pages, and stores the new answers; `--form` walks every dependent choice of
the bid form (it never signs). Run it before a testing session and after every agent run that left a
`_missing.log`; restart the mirror afterwards. `captured/_refresh.json` holds the last report, with the scenario
and challenge version it saw.

## Browsers with DevTools

```sh
python3 sim/mirror.py &                                               # the mirror
uv run --project agent python sim/chrome.py 2                         # two browsers, prints CDP_URL / CDP_URLS
SIM_BROWSERS=4 dev/run-sim.sh v2 "attach like the sandbox"            # agent run that attaches over CDP
```

`chrome.py` opens 1 to 4 browsers, each with a Chrome DevTools port (9222 and up), the way the sandbox provides
them. Playwright attaches with `chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")`; Puppeteer, an MCP browser
server or the DevTools window (chrome://inspect, add `127.0.0.1:9222`) work the same way, also while an agent is
running in that browser.

`drive.py` prints each page the way the agent sees it (text with `[eN ...]` refs) and takes `goto`, `click`,
`fill`, `select`, `check`, `back`, `crawl`, `halt`, `label`, `open`. Every action is recorded. The run's login is
replaced by placeholders before anything is written.

## What to record

The mirror can only show what was recorded, so walk what an agent may reach:

- each website's link crawl, after passing its entry checks by hand;
- the specification's revisions and every page of their viewer;
- ERP: each catalogue group in each transaction's search help, then `crawl` from the result list;
- webmail: the tender reference with each record subject the brief's rules name, in each folder, every result
  page and every message; the reference alone and a too-broad word (the "more than 20 hits" page);
- the bid form: both ways through it (bid and decline), each position's choices, a position left out, a position
  added and removed, each mistake once (to record its message), a TAN requested twice, a wrong TAN, a signed
  bid. Sessions on the scouting login end without warning, so script the walk and keep it under a minute.

After an agent run, `sim/captured/_missing.log` lists every address the agent asked for that was not recorded.

## Exact, rebuilt, missing

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Exact | Every recorded page, byte for byte: markup, styles, scripts, nested frames, decoy buttons and popups, hidden text, tooltips, drawn labels. Checked by `test_recorded_pages_come_back_as_recorded` and `browser_check.py`. |
| Rebuilt from what the recording shows | Sign-in, cookie notice, entry checks with a fresh number each time, the error page shown before a page, session timeout (`SIM_SESSION_SECONDS`), the bid form (steps, dependent choices, messages, omitted and added positions, summary, TAN, receipt), TAN mails in the mailbox. The bid form is checked by replaying the recorded walks: every page must equal the one the website answered with. |
| Assumed, not observed | Going back inside the position steps; whether a lead time is required; the form's reaction to a stale revision counter; a refused sign-in. |
| Missing | Any search or address not recorded, dependent choices nobody walked, the ERP's command field. These answer with a "Not recorded" page, never with a guess. |

Things the websites place at random on every page (a popup's close button, the order of some lists and of the
form's positions) are random on the mirror too.

## Limits

- It mirrors the public scenario. The final run uses other software, layouts and data, so a fix that only helps
  here is overfitting: it must stay generic and also hold in a sandbox test run.
- Message counts on the mailbox start page are the recorded ones, also after the mirror handed out new TANs.
- The mirror does not score. `captured/_signed.json` holds the bids signed on it, in the form's own fields.

## Next

Scenarios with invented data in these exact pages (one per trap in the bid rules), an expected answer worked
out independently of `agent/calc.py`, and a scorer with the challenge's weights. The recorded pages then serve as
templates and `sim/captured/` still holds everything that came from the websites.

# Usage, from anywhere: dev/run-sim.sh <version> ["note"] [experiment]

note=${2:-}

## Context

The final ranking runs our latest passing submission on a private dataset with other software, layouts and data.

- **Teammate's synthetic dataset** (`origin/research/agent-architecture`, commit a94a0d4): `dev/synth/` with a seeded

  four public sites plus `dev/run-sim.sh`. It reproduces the real platform's hazards exactly but has no expected
  answer and no scorer. Its README names the missing piece: invented-data scenarios with an oracle and a scorer.

Goal: one branch, based on the latest `main`, where the team's current agent can be run against invented scenarios
that also carry the kinds of hazards the real platform has, and against our mirror, with every run scored or recorded.

Decisions taken without an answer from you (say so if either is wrong):

- "Our platform's traps" = the classes of hazard our mirror reproduces from the real sites and the synthetic sites
  lack. They are ported as generic, invented structures, never as copied markup, wording or values.
- The uncommitted v2 agent fixes in the current checkout are left untouched. The branch is built in a separate
  worktree; they do not apply to the v3 agent on main anyway.

137	    """An amount in whole cents over positions by weight: largest remainders, or round each and hand the
138	    difference to the largest weight. Ties go to the lower position number."""
139	    cents = int(money(amount) / CENT)

143	    if rule == "largest_remainder":
144	        share = {k: int(exact[k].to_integral_value(ROUND_FLOOR)) for k in order}
145	        for k in sorted(order, key=lambda k: exact[k] - share[k], reverse=True)[:cents - sum(share.values())]:
146	            share[k] += 1
147	    else:
148	        share = {k: int(exact[k].to_integral_value(ROUND_HALF_UP)) for k in order}
149	        share[max(order, key=lambda k: weights[k])] += cents - sum(share.values())
150	    return {k: D(v) * CENT for k, v in share.items()}
